title: Walking skeleton
head: 5474e8b
lede: An almost empty app that proves three things before any feature exists: the page renders without waiting for the network, a mocked REST API answers real fetch calls under the GitHub Pages base path, and CI gates the deploy. Read the diagram, then step through a scenario.

files.question: In what order does the app start?
files.summary: The composition root: renders, then starts the mock, then makes the first request.
files.owns: Startup order, and wiring the mock to the app.
files.never: Holds UI or knows how a request gets answered.

files.question: What does the user see?
files.summary: A static placeholder until the Board exists.
files.tested: Browser test in Chromium and Firefox.

files.question: Where is the API?
files.summary: Pure: turns the Vite base path into the API base URL.
files.owns: The URL rule, in one place.
files.never: Reads the environment or makes requests.
files.tested: Unit tests and a type test.

files.question: How does the mock get installed?
files.summary: Registers the MSW service worker under the base path.
files.owns: The worker URL, its scope, and what happens to unhandled requests.
files.never: Decides when to start, or what to answer.

files.question: What does the fake server answer?
files.summary: One route: GET notes returns an empty list.
files.owns: The responses of the mocked API.

files.question: Is the URL rule right?
files.summary: Checks the rule for the Pages path and for the root.
files.never: Starts a browser or a worker.

files.question: Does the page render?
files.summary: Renders App alone in real browsers.
files.owns: The smoke test for the placeholder.
files.never: Runs main.tsx, so it never starts MSW.

files.question: How is it built and tested?
files.summary: The base path, the two test projects and the coverage gate.
files.tested: Exercised by every build and test run.

files.question: What must pass before a deploy?
files.summary: One workflow: check, then deploy from main.
files.owns: The gate and the Pages deploy.

steps.title: The browser runs the entry module
steps.explain: `main.tsx` finds `#root` and asks React to render App. This comes first on purpose: nothing above it waits for the network, so a slow mock can never leave a blank page.

steps.title: The mock code downloads as its own chunk
steps.explain: The dynamic `import()` makes Vite split MSW into a separate file. The module pauses at this `await`, and React can paint meanwhile.

steps.title: The API address is computed
steps.explain: `BASE_URL` is `/sticky-notes/`, from the `base` option in the Vite config, so the API base is `/sticky-notes/api`. The function takes the base as an argument instead of reading the environment, which is why a plain Node test can cover it.

steps.title: The service worker registers
steps.explain: The worker script and its scope both sit under `/sticky-notes/`. The scope decides **which pages** the worker controls. The handlers are built here, from the same API base that the fetch will use.

steps.title: The first GET goes out
steps.explain: It is sent only now, because `main.tsx` awaited the worker. Sent earlier, it could go straight to GitHub Pages, which has no API. It is a real fetch, so it shows in the DevTools Network tab.

steps.title: The handler answers 200 and an empty list
steps.explain: The worker passes the request to the handler in the page, and the response returns through the worker. The console prints `GET /notes → 200 []`. Nothing stores it yet.

steps.title: The app is running, and something fetches /sticky-notes/api/nope
steps.explain: The worker sees the request, because it comes from a page it controls. Only GET notes has a handler, so none matches.

steps.title: MSW lets it through to the real server
steps.explain: `bypass` means no warning and no fake error. The local preview server answered **200 with HTML**, its fallback page. So a forgotten handler looks like a success until `response.json()` throws.

steps.title: The page renders as usual
steps.explain: Rendering happened before any mock code ran, so the failure cannot take it back.

steps.title: Registration is blocked, and start() rejects
steps.explain: Reproduced by blocking service workers in both browsers: MSW throws `Failed to register the Service Worker`.

steps.title: Startup stops there
steps.explain: Nothing catches the rejection, so the GET is never sent and the only sign is an uncaught error in the console. That is harmless for a placeholder. Once Notes are saved through this API, it needs handling.

steps.title: A pull request or a push to main starts CI
steps.explain: Both run the same check job. Typecheck and lint come first because they are the cheapest to fail.

steps.title: Unit tests run in Node
steps.explain: They cover pure code, such as the URL rule, without a browser.

steps.title: Browser tests run in Chromium and Firefox
steps.explain: This one renders App by itself. It does **not** run `main.tsx`, so green tests say nothing about the worker or the GET.

steps.title: Coverage and build
steps.explain: The 90% gate applies only to the pure-core folders. Components are left to the browser tests.

steps.title: Deploy, from main only
steps.explain: A pull request stops after the check job. On main, or a manual run on main, the built folder is published to GitHub Pages. `needs: check` blocks a deploy when the gate is red. Only the push-to-main path has run so far: the pull request and red-gate paths come from reading the workflow.

notes.title: A comment at this commit is false.
notes.detail: `apiBaseUrl.ts` says the API must be under the base path to stay inside the worker scope, and its unit test name repeats that. Scope limits which pages are controlled, not which URLs they can fetch. With the API moved to `/api`, MSW still answered 200 in Chromium and Firefox. The base path is still a tidy choice, but not for that reason. The comment and test name were corrected in the PR that introduced walkthroughs.

notes.title: The mock ships to production.
notes.detail: That is deliberate (ADR 0002): there is no backend. The counter-argument is that it adds weight and a point of failure to the live site. The separate chunk answers the first half, but not the second.

notes.title: The startup wiring has no automated test.
notes.detail: The tests cover the URL rule and App. The order in `main.tsx`, the worker and the handler could all break with CI green.

notes.title: MSW 3 renamed an option.
notes.detail: The issue says `onUnhandledRequest`. The code uses `onUnhandledFrame`, its new name.
